## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the rename fixes the migration-marker collision described in #12173. At the base, an account holding a `1789095456.sh` completion marker from the deleted Panther Lake (PTL) kernel migration never runs the Mise Work PATH cleanup from #11336. At this head, the renamed `1789584463.sh` is pending for that account and removes the unsafe config. No correctness issue was found in the two-file change.

```text
Synthetic account: stock ~/Work/.mise.toml, trusted, PTL-era 1789095456.sh marker
Real bin/omarchy-migrate from each tree, mise 2026.9.4

                        base 45748a28                 head 72c37a91
omarchy-migrate         nothing pending, no run       runs 1789584463.sh, marks it
~/Work/.mise.toml       kept, still trusted           removed
mise env in a ~/Work    exports <repo>/bin on PATH    recreated stock config is
repository                                            rejected as untrusted
```

**Verified:** the affected population is wider than PTL hardware. The PTL migration began with `omarchy-pkg-present linux-ptl || exit 0`, and `omarchy-migrate` records any zero exit as complete. So every account that ran migrations from a `quattro` tree between 2026-09-13 18:51Z and 2026-09-14 20:49Z holds the marker, on any machine. First-install provisioning from that window marks shipped migrations complete the same way (source reading). The PTL migration is not in any tag or release branch, so this concerns edge and development-checkout users.

**Verified:** the renamed file is byte-identical to the old one, `1789584463` appears nowhere else in the fetched branch and tag history, and the remaining `1789095456` references (the comment in `migrations/1789325478.sh` and the old-world simulation in `omarchy-kernel-migration-test.sh`) correctly name the historical PTL migration. On the PR's base, `omarchy-kernel-migration-test.sh` fails at the quoted "superseded migration" assertion and passes at head. `mise-work-path-test.sh` passes at base and head, and a copy of the head test pointed back at the old path fails at the first migration call, so the test does run the renamed file.

### Re-running the cleanup is not a no-op for re-trusted custom Work configs

The description says the one-day overlap population "simply re-runs a no-op". Two groups are involved, and they behave differently:

- Accounts holding only the PTL-era marker run the cleanup for the first time (the fix above).
- Accounts that already ran the Mise cleanup under `1789095456` (on `quattro` since 2026-09-15) run it again under the new id. With a stock config, the re-run left the synthetic home unchanged apart from the new marker. With a custom `~/Work/.mise.toml` that the user trusted again after the first run, as the migration's own message invites, the re-run revokes that trust again and prints the revocation message again.

**Impact:** for that second case, mise warns that `~/Work/.mise.toml` is not trusted and applies none of its settings until the user runs `mise trust` again. The effect is conservative (trust is removed, never granted) and limited to edge and development accounts. A marker cannot distinguish a PTL-era run from a Mise-era run, so the code has no clean way to avoid it.

**Suggested change:** reword the description so maintainers accept this knowingly: PTL-marker holders run the cleanup for the first time, and accounts that already ran it get a re-run that is a no-op for stock configs but revokes a re-granted trust on a custom Work config once more. No code change is suggested.

**Current `quattro` context:** `faffb8ee` has since removed the kernel-test assertion quoted in the description, so on current `quattro` the rename no longer changes that test's result. The user-facing reason still applies, because current `quattro` still ships the Mise cleanup as `migrations/1789095456.sh`. Separately, `omarchy-kernel-migration-test.sh` fails on current `quattro` with or without this PR: #11495 made the `omarchy-pkg-*` helpers pass `--` to pacman, while the test's pacman stub still reads `$2` for `-Q` and its call-log check for the new kernel packages expects the old `pacman -S` command line. The "both suites pass" result therefore holds on the PR's original base, not after a rebase.

**Test scope:** Source review of base `45748a28`, head `72c37a91` and current `quattro` `d201fb95`, including Git history and tags. Both repository tests ran in an isolated sandbox on base and head, and on current `quattro` with and without this change. Migration scenarios ran each tree's real `bin/omarchy-migrate` against synthetic home directories with mise 2026.9.4 and only the Mise cleanup migration installed. The PTL marker was created directly, not by running the deleted migration.
